output.brief: The gap is mostly a difference in length of service, not work location. Remote hiring only opened widely in July 2024, so 230 of 340 remote staff (68%) don't yet have the 18 months in level that the policy requires. Only 26% of office staff are in that position. Among people who are eligible, the promotion rates are almost the same: 21.1% for office and 20.0% for remote. Applying the office rates to the remote group's tenure mix predicts 8.2%, against the 7.6% seen. Remote staff leave at no higher a rate than office staff, and the gap appears in every job family, so neither attrition nor job-family mix explains it. Proximity bias isn't proven, but it isn't ruled out either. Only 110 remote employees are eligible, so a difference of a few points either way can't be excluded. Manager comments about handing urgent work to nearby staff are anecdotes, not measurements. Don't adopt the three-day office rule. It rests on a misread of the data, and it would hit the roughly 180 remote staff hired on home-based contracts. Instead, report promotion rates for eligible staff only, and re-check at FY2027. Meanwhile, collect stretch-assignment data (X7) to test the visibility concern directly. I'm fairly confident in this, though not certain.
